title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction:
Opening page of E449, Euler's 1774 paper on residues of powers modulo a prime. Euler fixes a prime P and an integer a. He considers the geometric progression 1, a, a^2, a^3, ... and calls the least non-negative residues of its terms mod P by the names 1, α, β, γ, δ, ε, ζ, ... (§1). In modern terms he is studying the sequence a^k mod P, i.e. the cyclic subgroup generated by a in (Z/PZ)^*.

§2 states that every residue is less than P. While a^k < P the residue is the term itself. Once a^k ≥ P, one subtracts P as often as possible, which leaves a remainder smaller than P. This is the division algorithm.

§3 begins on this page and finishes on the next. If gcd(a, P) = 1, no power of a is divisible by P, so 0 never occurs among the residues. This is Euclid's lemma for a prime P.

The page serves as the setup for the rest of the paper. The following sections show that residues recur (pigeonhole), that each residue is obtained from the previous one by multiplying by a and reducing, and that the integers fall into residue classes. Later in the paper Euler treats the period of a mod P and Fermat's little theorem, and makes his attempt to show that a primitive root exists for every prime.

ideas.what: Sequence of residues of a geometric progression a^k modulo a prime P
ideas.modern_name: Powers of a in (Z/PZ)^*; the cyclic subgroup generated by a
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E262, E271, E449); later systematized by Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), Section III
ideas.where_published: E262 'Theoremata circa residua ex divisione potestatum relicta' (1761); E449 (this paper)

ideas.what: Residues are less than the divisor P
If a is coprime to the prime P, no power of a is divisible by P

deep.surprise_reason: This is the title page and elementary setup (definitions, the division algorithm, a coprime base never giving residue 0). It repeats Euler's own earlier E262 and is well documented in the literature on Euler's primitive root argument.
transcription_corrections: The third residue letter is printed as the curly beta 'ϐ' (rendered β in the transcription), which is correct in meaning.
The ornament '( o )' in the running head is the printer's decoration, not text.
